aim: Does the biological reproductive-versus-vegetative organ grouping describe higher phylogenetic K across plant families on identical species/tips, and can it predict held-out plant family trait-ordering without peeking at that family's K?

provenance.discovery_status: All original K, 760 matched-tip K and their focal-trait profile outcomes were observed before selecting this broad functional module interpretation; this is exploratory model-adequacy and predictive generalization, NOT prospective discovery.

fixed_organ_classes.seed_height: Not in 249-system original K-blind source-calibratable subgraph; never added

matched_tip.reproductive_vegetative_comparison: For every supported family×pair where exactly one trait is reproductive, record 1 if reproductive K>vegetative K, else 0. Pair types and family rows remain dependent.
summarize: pair-weighted reproductive K higher proportion; family resampling 95% CI
equal-family mean proportion; family resampling 95% CI
all 36 cross-module pair-types equal-weight, and descriptive >=5-family pair type rate
only fruits versus vegetative, only seeds versus vegetative, excluding seed_dry_mass, excluding leaf_area, leave-one-named-trait-out min/max
joint S3/prune axis agreement where both available

predictive_models.validation: Leave ONE WHOLE plant family out, fit entirely on all OTHER families; score held-out family rows. Never train on any K outcome in the held-out family.
predictive_models.baseline: Smoothed pooled other-family positive lexical-order rate, (n_positive+1)/(n+2). Inherently a label-order baseline, not a biological causal null.
predictive_models.module: Fixed biological module contrast +1 if trait A reproductive and B vegetative, -1 if reversed, 0 if same module; sklearn ridge logistic regression C=1.0, no intercept, fixed solver lbfgs, no hyperparameter tuning.
predictive_models.named_trait: 12-trait Bradley-Terry-style logistic features +1 for trait A, -1 for trait B, ridge logistic C=1.0, no intercept; a family-agnostic transitive prior across PAIR-SPECIFIC taxon cohorts, not proof of a universal shared-species 12-trait hierarchy.
predictive_models.saturated_pair: Same named-trait pair positive-rank direction in OTHER families, Laplace-smoothed (positives+1)/(training families+2), defaults to 0.5 for a pair not observed in any other family.
accurate_scores: hard sign accuracy with 0.5 credit for ties
score_slices: named pair types with >=5 supported families

original_source_OU_process_null.aim: Different null question on the ORIGINAL separate-tip 249 system K graph, not the matched-tip graph: Does homogeneous OU plus fixed K-blind source-associated observational noise predict how often reproductive morphology outranks vegetative morphology?
statistics: pair-weighted cross-module reproductive-higher fraction on original separate tip source K
equal-family reproductive-higher fraction over families with at least one cross-module comparison
original_source_OU_process_null.simulated_tail: Conditional posterior-predictive descriptive Monte Carlo (1 + #sim>=observed)/257 and q2.5/q97.5; module label grouping selected post-outcome and multiple correlated scenarios must NOT be treated as independent confirmations.
original_source_OU_process_null.not_same_tip: Do not directly compare the original-separate-taxon OU null distribution to the matched-taxon observed module percentage; compare each null only to its exact observed original 249-graph counterpart.

hard_nonclaims: This entire module hypothesis was articulated after seeing named-trait hierarchy and 760 pairwise results. No preregistered confirmatory p-value can be claimed.
Phenological/developmental evolutionary constraints, species-specific OU alpha and natural selection are not identified by Blomberg K or class contrasts.
Matched identical taxa/trees do not equalize observation quality, source provenance, measurement protocols or phylogenetic trait covariance.
Multinomial correlations among within-family and pair-specific observations require family-clustered uncertainty; source datasets can span multiple plant families.
A common module is a predictor of K on the retained sampling graph, not proof of one universal K ordering on a common 12-trait taxon set.
Source OU process null may be misspecified and uses original separate taxon supports; even a poor module posterior-predictive fit does not imply adaptive/selection mechanism.
No independent TRY v7 primary measurement dataset has passed provenance checks; do not reopen closed BIEN 201-system rho analysis.
